answer: Personhood nullifiers tie every agent to one accountable operator. To register, the operator proves in zero knowledge that they hold a unique credential, and the proof emits a nullifier, a fixed tag that is the same at every vertex of the network but reveals nothing else. A second agent from the same credential produces the same tag, like a mirror showing one face twice, and is rejected. An attacker needs a fresh real credential per fake, each costly to obtain and as hard to forge as eroding karst rock.
